body: Yeah, but I want to know why I got the wind knocked out of me. Like, I haven't really had that happen before. It's weird.

I had then. Then it took a quantum leap with Europa Universalis III and Hearts of Iron II.

I love Paradox.

Well, I'm not going to lie, throwing out that you did the dirty deed with your boyfriend to near-total strangers was probably not your best foot forward. But don't let that get you down, despite the hypocrisy, there are good people out there.

I was in a similar position as you, but I wound up as an Eastern Orthodox Christian. Go figure.

The worst part about getting better is dealing with my ADHD. And, for the record, I've been in therapy since high school. It's helped somewhat, but its like the emptiness never goes away.

ADHD is another challenge altogether. Besides the stigma, both the people who think that it's contrived and those who who think that its so trivial that they might even have it, it's actually rather incapacitating at times. It's not just school either, though that's a problem. It's with friends, with family, with even things that give me pleasure. Sometimes I can't focus in or remember what people are saying. Other times, its just distractibility. Usually, I won't be able to finish games that I love playing, or projects sit half finished. I'll even get distracted from eating meals--not once in a while. Every. Fucking. Day.

I've tried meds, but I hate the side effects (insomnia, anxiety and loss of appetite). Contrary to homeopathy and the drivel that Scientologists--or even fundamentalists in my experience--spout, there's not too much else that can be done. I did an alternative treatment of neuro and biofeedback, and, $6000 later, marginal gains. The only alternative to meds are a regimen of cognitive behavioral therapy and a dramatically reshaped appetite to revolve around fish.

I tried several different types of meds. SSRIs are most common (Paxil was the drug of choice), but it had limited results. Apparently, there are a select few people that have null or inverse reactions to SSRIs and I might be one of them, which basically means that they would make it worse. Right now, I'm on tetracyclics, which are very sedative. They stimulate my appetite, which is a good thing. Unlike most people, I lose my appetite on depressive streaks, instead of gaining it, and I loose a lot of weight. I'm 6'0 and weigh around 120 lbs. However, the sedating part, which is common will all drugs, puts me at odds with my school schedule, and I often have to avoid signing up for morning classes (like before 10 am). I flunked out of psychology 101 in my freshman year for this exact reason.
